title: Keys, not coins
hook: You download a wallet app. It shows you 12 random words and says: "Write these down. Anyone with these words can take your coins." Wait, what?
card1: A [[wallet]] doesn't really hold coins. The coins are recorded on the [[blockchain]]. The wallet holds the keys that let you move them.
analogy1: Your private key is like the key to a glass mailbox on a busy street. Everyone can see the mailbox and drop coins in, but only the key opens it.
card2: Your [[seed-phrase]] is a backup of all your keys. If you lose your phone, the 12 or 24 words bring your wallet back. If someone else gets them, they get your coins.
card3: With some apps, a company holds the keys for you, a bit like a bank. That's easier, but you have to trust the company. With your own wallet you hold the keys, and nobody can help if you lose them.
adviceIntro: Someone in a forum shares tips for keeping a seed phrase safe. Which tips are bad?

l1.text: Take a photo of it so you don't lose it.
l1.why: Photos get backed up to the cloud and can be hacked or found. Use paper, kept offline.

l2.text: Write it on paper and keep it somewhere safe at home.
l2.why: Paper can't be hacked. Some people keep a second copy in another safe place.

l3.text: Email it to yourself so you always have it.
l3.why: Email accounts get hacked. Anything online can leak.

l4.text: Never type it into a website, even if it looks official.
l4.why: You only ever type it into your wallet app itself, when you restore the wallet.

l5.text: Split it with a friend so each of you keeps half.
l5.why: Half a phrase is much easier to guess, and now you depend on someone else.

setup.prompt: Your new wallet app shows your 12-word seed phrase and asks you to save it.

screenshot.label: Take a screenshot
screenshot.before: You will save the words as a picture on your phone.
screenshot.what: Months later, a game you installed had harmful code that read your photos. Your practice coins were taken.
screenshot.why: Screenshots end up in photo libraries and cloud backups that other apps and hackers can reach.
screenshot.how: Some harmful apps search photos for seed phrases. One picture is enough.
screenshot.realLife: Never keep your seed phrase as a photo, a screenshot, a note or a message.

later.label: Skip it and do it later
later.before: You will skip the backup for now.
later.what: Your phone broke a week later. Without the words the wallet can't be restored, and the practice coins are lost.
later.why: The seed phrase is the only backup. No company can reset it for you.
later.how: Your own wallet has no "forgot password" button. The keys exist only on your device and in the seed phrase.
later.realLife: Write the seed phrase down right away, before you put any coins in.

paper.label: Write it on paper and keep it safe at home
paper.before: You will copy the 12 words onto paper, in order.
paper.what: Your phone broke a week later. You typed the 12 words into a new phone, and your wallet came back.
paper.why: Paper stays offline, so it can't be hacked, and it lets you restore your wallet.
paper.how: The same words always rebuild the same keys, in any compatible wallet.
paper.realLife: Keep the paper somewhere safe and private, and check that you copied every word correctly.

q1.prompt: Where are your coins actually kept?
q1.b: On the blockchain. The wallet holds the keys to move them
q1.explanation: Coins live on the blockchain. Your wallet holds the private keys that let you move them.

q2.prompt: You lose your phone with your own wallet on it. What gets your coins back?
q2.a: The app's support team can reset it
q2.b: Your seed phrase, typed into a wallet on a new device
q2.explanation: The seed phrase is the backup of all your keys. Keep it safe and offline, and only type it into your wallet app when you restore it.

q3.prompt: What is the best way to keep a seed phrase?
q3.a: A photo, as long as the phone has a lock
q3.b: In a notes app or a cloud file
q3.c: Written on paper, kept somewhere safe and private
q3.explanation: Paper kept offline can't be hacked. Never store the phrase as a photo, a note or a message.

misc.coinsInPhone: "The coins are inside my phone." The phone only holds keys. The coins are recorded on the blockchain.
misc.coinsAtCompany: "The wallet company keeps my coins." With your own wallet, no company holds them. The record is on the blockchain.
misc.supportReset: "Support can reset my wallet." Nobody can reset your own wallet. Only the seed phrase restores it.
misc.passwordRestores: "My phone password brings it back." That password only unlocks that phone. The seed phrase restores the wallet.
misc.photoSafe: "A photo is safe if my phone is locked." Photos get backed up and shared with apps. Paper kept offline is safer.
misc.cloudNote: "A notes app or cloud file is fine." Anything online can leak or be hacked.

t1: A [[wallet]] holds keys. The coins are on the [[blockchain]].
t2: Your [[seed-phrase]] is the backup of everything. Write it on paper and keep it offline.
t3: Nobody can reset your own wallet for you. If a company holds the keys, you have to trust that company.
talk1: Where at home would be a safe and private place to keep something important on paper?
talk2: Would you rather hold your own keys or let a company hold them? What are the pros and cons?
